target_customer: Industrial and logistics operators deploying collaborative robots, initially for picking and packing, with ABB Robotics as a channel partner
problem: Industrial robots need slow, brittle programming and downtime for each new task, so Mbodi lets operators teach skills with language and short demonstrations.
business_model: B2B robot software and agents sold with partners such as ABB; pricing not public
product_category: Embodied AI and robot skill learning for industrial automation

founders.name: Sebastian Peralta
education: University of Pennsylvania, triple major EE, CS and Physics; graduate research at the GRASP Robotics Lab

founders.name: Xavier (Tianhao) Chi
education: UIUC, bachelor's and master's in ECE

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable language-driven robot skill learning in production needs perception, planning and control to work together on physical hardware.

defensibility.rationale: Skills shared across a fleet and an ABB partnership create some lock-in, but robot foundation model labs are well funded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: ABB chose partnership: Mbodi won ABB's AI Startup Challenge and signed a joint commercialization agreement.

market_need_then: Industrial robots remain hard to reprogram while generative AI advanced; the founders cite brittle code and long deployment cycles as the pain.

identity.logo: updated logo announced with the line 'new look, same mission' per a third-party profile, not verified
identity.voice_and_tone: confident and direct with punchy lines such as 'Work moves fast. Robots haven't.'

branding.brand_signature: Live robot demos on stage at TechCrunch Startup Battlefield
branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch podcast appearances and a Startup Battlefield demo, plus Business Insider and Automate challenge recognition

brand_strength.rationale: Some press from TechCrunch and industry awards, but the name is unusual and no brand pages or community were found.

outcome_analysis: Mbodi has early traction signals: an ABB commercialization agreement after ABB's AI Startup Challenge, a pharma pilot reported in 2026 and the Automate 2026 Startup Challenge win. Its funding is not verifiable from primary sources, and well-funded robot foundation model players raise the competitive bar. The story is still early and no failure or exit has been reported.
notes: Aggregators report about $500K to $625K raised with investors such as Betaworks, Network VC, ZAKA VC, Founders Capital and Pioneer Fund, and a TechCrunch Battlefield profile lists $500,000; one outlet claims a First Round led seed. None is a primary or corroborated round, so no round is recorded. Competitor list left empty because no source dated near the Spring 2025 batch was found; an aggregator naming T-Robotics, Skild AI and Figure AI is low quality. One aggregator places the batch at W24 versus Spring 2025 on YC. The ABB agreement date was not found.
